title: Sermo I opening: today's joy, David's oracle, and Gabriel's hail
english: He makes plain to us the mystery that was hidden from eternity. Today crowns of lasting virtue are woven. Today God, wanting to crown the heads of the kind and devout and of those who carefully keep feast days, names the lovers of firm faith as called ones and heirs; and with eagerness He calls those who set their mind on heavenly things into the upper kingdom, so that they may join themselves to the divine ministry of the bodiless choirs.

Today David's oracle is fulfilled, which says: Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth exult. The fields will be glad, and all the trees of the wood, at the sight of the Lord, for He comes (Psalm 96:11-13). David indeed says trees; but the Forerunner of the Lord names trees that bear fruit worthy of repentance — rather, worthy of the Lord's coming. And our Lord Jesus Christ announces lasting joy to all who believe in Him. For He says: I will see you, and you will rejoice; and your joy no one will take from you (John 16:22).

Today the famous and unspeakable joy of Christians, who have set their hope on Christ, is announced. Today Gabriel, who stands before God, coming to the most chaste Virgin, announces to her that word: Hail, full of grace (Luke 1:28). And while she was thinking within herself what sort of greeting that might be, the Angel at once added, saying: The Lord is with you. Do not fear, Mary; for you have found favor with God. Therefore you will conceive in the womb and bear a son; and they will call His name Jesus. He will be great, and will be called the Son of the Most High. And the Lord will give Him the throne of David His father, and He will reign in the house of Jacob forever; and of His kingdom there will be no end (Luke 1:30-33).

But Mary said to the Angel: How will this be done to me, since I do not know a man? (Luke 1:34). While the most holy Virgin was turning this over in her mind as if in wonder, the Angel briefly brings the speech to its close and says: The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. And therefore the holy one who will be born of you will also be called the Son of God (Luke 1:35). For what He is, that He will entirely be called. Fittingly, then, he marks out holy Mary alone from among all generations.
